title: metadata-04: i;unicode-casemap for metadataTextContains
description:
draft-ietf-jmap-metadata-04 specifies the RFC 5051 collation for metadataTextContains.

-04 §3.6 metadataTextContains: "Matches an object if the metadata value at the supplied path is a string that contains the supplied value as a substring under the "i;unicode-casemap" collation [RFC5051]."
-04 §3.6 metadataTextEquals: "is exactly equal to the supplied value, comparing Unicode code points without case folding or normalization."
(-02: "case-insensitive substring" with no collation named; equals was "case-sensitive, byte-for-byte".)

Affected:
- crate-jmap-metadata-server/src/filter.rs:116-120 metadata_text_contains uses str::to_lowercase on both sides. That is not i;unicode-casemap: RFC 5051 §2 titlecases each character, then applies NFKD decomposition, then compares. Example: U+FB01 LATIN SMALL LIGATURE FI should match "fi" under RFC 5051 but does not under to_lowercase.
- unicode-normalization is already in Cargo.lock (line ~3360, transitive). Check that it is acceptable as a direct dependency of jmap-metadata-server before adding it.
- Tests need an external oracle: the RFC 5051 algorithm applied by hand to fixed vectors (for example, ligature and compatibility characters), or Dovecot/Cyrus i;unicode-casemap output.
- crate-jmap-metadata-server/src/filter.rs:122-150 metadata_text_equals: Rust == on str compares code points, so no code change. Update the "byte-for-byte" doc wording to the -04 wording.
- crate-jmap-metadata-types/src/filter.rs:135 and :143 field docs: update the wording.

No signature change.
